on_login.reason: Flet Page.on_login is emitted by the backend authentication flow after the auth service completes; it is not a platform-view event and the Apple renderer must not synthesize it. Ruflet's server/session layer owns this callback exactly as Flet's Python backend does.

on_logout.reason: Flet Page.on_logout is emitted by the backend authentication flow when credentials are cleared; it is not a native Apple UI event. Ruflet's server/session auth layer owns it, matching the Flet backend contract.

barrier_color.reason: SwiftUI's system sheet API does not expose the native modal dimming-view color on the iOS 15/macOS 13.1 deployment floor. presentationBackground changes the picker surface, not the barrier, so the Apple renderer deliberately leaves the system barrier intact instead of falsely applying this color to the wrong element.

enable_ime_personalized_learning.reason: Flutter applies this only on Android. Its own TextInputConfiguration documents it as 'This flag only affects Android. On iOS, there is no equivalent flag.', and it maps to IME_FLAG_NO_PERSONALIZED_LEARNING. Ignoring it is what the Flutter engine does on Apple, so ignoring it here is exact parity rather than a gap.

android_options.reason: FlutterSecureStorage selects only the options map for the running platform. The Apple renderer consumes ios_options/macos_options and, exactly like Flutter on Apple, does not apply Android storage options.

web_options.reason: FlutterSecureStorage selects only the options map for the running platform. The Apple renderer uses Keychain options and does not instantiate the web storage backend.

windows_options.reason: FlutterSecureStorage selects only the options map for the running platform. The Apple renderer uses Keychain options and does not instantiate the Windows storage backend.
